chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Venmo Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with where the money needs to end up. Zelle sends directly between eligible United States (US) bank accounts, so there is no separate wallet balance or instant cash-out fee. Venmo, PayPal and Apple Cash offer $0 standard withdrawals, while their instant withdrawals carry a percentage fee.

Next, separate the cost of sending from the cost of receiving. Venmo charges 3.00% for a credit-card-funded personal send, while a debit-card-funded domestic personal send costs $0. PayPal charges 2.90% + $0.30 for domestic personal sends funded by a credit card or a debit card other than the PayPal Debit Card. For more on cash advances, see the [credit card cash advance guide](/guides/credit-card-cash-advance-guide/).

A payment for goods has different economics from a personal transfer. Venmo's personal-profile goods-and-services fee is 2.99% to the recipient, its standard Business Profile rate is 1.9% + $0.10, and Square prices card acceptance by plan and payment method. When sending across borders, add both the transfer fee and the currency conversion spread.

Run through these five checks before picking an app:

- Does the recipient have an eligible US bank account, a compatible device or a required wallet?
- Will you fund the send from a bank, balance, debit card or credit card?
- Do you need funds in an external bank immediately, or can you wait for a $0 standard transfer?
- Is the payment personal, a sale, a donation or an international transfer?
- For a sale, will the customer pay in person, by invoice or through a wallet?

For customer invoices, the [invoicing apps for freelancers](/roundup/best-invoicing-apps-for-freelancers/) roundup covers dedicated billing tools. Zelle's homepage and consumer fee page publish no dollar sending limits and advise checking with your financial institution.

alternatives.heading: Zelle Direct Bank Transfers and Fee Structure
alternatives.body:
Zelle sends domestic personal payments directly between eligible bank accounts inside more than 2,400 US bank and credit union apps and online banking portals. Zelle notes there are typically no consumer fees to send or receive, and advises confirming with your bank or credit union. A first-quarter 2026 survey on Zelle's site found $0 send, receive and request fees at 99.40% of linked consumer checking and savings accounts.

Both people need eligible US checking or savings accounts, so Zelle does not send money internationally. For enrolled recipients, money typically moves between bank accounts within minutes with no wallet balance to withdraw and no 1.75% instant cash-out fee. Zelle's homepage and consumer fee page publish no dollar sending limits.

A $1,000 rent payment illustrates the math. Receiving $1,000 through Zelle at a fee-free linked bank puts $1,000 directly into the recipient's checking account for $0 in transfer fees.

Receiving $1,000 through Venmo and cashing out immediately costs 1.75%, or $17.50, totaling $210 across 12 monthly rent payments. Zelle fits domestic bank-to-bank transfers, though payments to enrolled recipients cannot be canceled or reversed once sent (cancellation works only before a recipient enrolls).

alternatives.heading: PayPal Personal, Card and International Fees
alternatives.body:
PayPal offers a separate wallet for domestic personal payments and international sends, with a card-funding rule that differs from Venmo's. A domestic Friends and Family payment funded by a PayPal balance, PayPal Debit Card, linked bank account or American Express Send Account costs $0. Funding a domestic personal send with a credit card or another debit card costs 2.90% + $0.30, while receiving a personal payment without currency conversion costs $0.

A standard withdrawal to a linked bank account or eligible debit card costs $0, and an instant withdrawal costs 1.75% ($0.25 minimum, $25 maximum). Paper-check withdrawals cost $1.50 on accounts without a PayPal Balance account.

For international personal sends, PayPal adds 5.00% ($0.99 minimum, $4.99 maximum) on top of any domestic funding fee. Currency conversion adds a 4.00% spread when a personal or Payouts recipient gets another currency or on foreign-currency purchases, and 3.00% on other conversions unless another rate is disclosed.

On a $500 domestic credit-card-funded personal send, Venmo's 3.00% fee is $15, whereas PayPal's 2.90% ($14.50) plus $0.30 totals $14.80. PayPal saves $0.20 on that credit-card send. By contrast, funding a domestic personal send with a non-PayPal debit card costs $0 on Venmo versus 2.90% + $0.30 on PayPal.

PayPal fits people who want wallet payments or its international personal-send route. PayPal also charges 2.89% + $0.49 to receive a domestic donation (plus 1.50% international), and its cryptocurrency buy and sell tiers run from 2.20% to 1.50%.

alternatives.heading: Apple Cash Instant Transfer Rates and Device Limits
alternatives.body:
Apple Cash provides $0 personal sends between compatible Apple devices and a slightly lower instant-transfer percentage than Venmo. It works in Wallet and Messages on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Apple Vision Pro. Green Dot Bank and Apple Payments Inc. provide the service, with Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) coverage up to $250,000 on registered cards.

Apple Cash lists no monthly, purchase, customer-service or inactivity fee, and offers no overdraft or credit feature. Sending or receiving a personal payment funded by an Apple Cash balance or debit card in Wallet costs $0. A standard Automated Clearing House (ACH) bank transfer costs $0 in one to three business days, while an instant debit-card transfer costs 1.7% rounded to the nearest cent ($0.25 minimum, $25 maximum).

For an $800 instant debit-card withdrawal, Apple Cash charges 1.7% ($13.60) versus Venmo's 1.75% ($14), saving $0.40. At larger amounts, each schedule hits its $25 fee cap: with nearest-cent rounding, Apple Cash reaches $25 at $1,470.30 ($1,470.59 unrounded), while Venmo's 1.75% reaches $25 at $1,428.58 unrounded.

Apple Cash fits people whose sender and recipient both use Apple devices and fund personal payments with a balance or debit card. Credit-card funding is unavailable for personal sends, and Android or Windows users cannot send or receive Apple Cash. Apple Cash terms also prohibit business or commercial use.

alternatives.heading: Wise Multi-Currency Transfers and Card Pricing
alternatives.body:
Wise is a Venmo alternative built for moving money between currencies rather than splitting a domestic dinner tab. Registration, holding balances and sending the same currency between Wise contacts all cost $0. Sending or converting between currencies starts at 0.23%, varies by currency pair and uses the mid-market exchange rate. Wise charges no monthly subscription fee.

Wise provides free account details for receiving in 22 currencies, with free non-wire domestic receipt in nine currencies: Australian dollars, Canadian dollars, euros, British pounds, Hungarian forints, New Zealand dollars, Philippine pesos, Singapore dollars and US dollars. Receiving a US dollar wire or Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) payment costs $6.11, while British pound and euro SWIFT receipts cost £2.16 and €2.39.

Getting a Wise Multi-Currency Card costs $9, with no subscription fees and $0 to spend a currency already held. Automated teller machine (ATM) withdrawals are free through $250 per calendar month and cost $1.95 + 1.95% per withdrawal above that threshold, while topping up certain external e-wallets costs 2%.

On a $1,000 conversion at Wise's starting 0.23% rate, the fee is $2.30, though other currency pairs can cost more. A $1,000 Venmo send to an eligible non-US PayPal account can incur Venmo's capped $4.99 international fee plus a 4.00% conversion spread ($40), totaling $44.99. Wise fits cross-currency transfers, whereas Venmo offers $0 eligible domestic personal sends, a $0 debit card and $0 US MoneyPass ATM withdrawals.

alternatives.heading: Square Business Processing Among Venmo Alternatives
alternatives.body:
Square serves sellers who need card acceptance and customer invoices rather than personal peer-to-peer transfers. Square Free costs $0 per month per location, Plus costs $49 and Premium costs $149, with 30-day free trials on Plus and Premium and custom pricing above $250,000 in annual card volume. In-person tap, dip or swipe payments cost 2.6% + $0.15 on Free, 2.5% + $0.15 on Plus and 2.4% + $0.15 on Premium.

Online and invoice card payments cost 3.3% + $0.30 on Free or 2.9% + $0.30 on Plus and Premium. Invoice payments by ACH cost 1% with a $1 minimum, uncapped on Free and capped at $10 on Plus and Premium. ACH transfers through Square's web and payments application programming interfaces (APIs) cost 1% with a $1 minimum and a $5 cap across all tiers.

Next-business-day external bank transfers cost $0, while instant external-bank transfers carry an unitemized fee on Square's pricing page. Square Checking is a free business checking account that gives instant debit-card access to Square sales. Square Savings lists a 1.00% annual percentage yield (APY) on folder balances over $10 (APY as published on January 23, 2026), with $0 monthly fees and no minimum deposit to open.

International cards add a 1.5% surcharge, optional payroll starts at $35 monthly plus $6 per person paid, and point-of-sale hardware starts at $59. For 100 in-person $50 payments, Square Free costs $145 ($130 percentage plus $15 fixed) versus $105 on a Venmo Business Profile at 1.9% + $0.10.

Square fits sellers who want major card acceptance and invoicing without requiring buyers to hold Venmo. The [business bank accounts roundup](/roundup/best-business-bank-accounts/) covers dedicated business checking options separately.

alternatives.heading: Xoom Cash Pickup and International Delivery
alternatives.body:
Xoom handles international delivery methods that domestic Venmo balance transfers do not cover. Operated by PayPal, Xoom delivers transfers to foreign bank accounts, debit cards and mobile wallets including India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Brazil's Pix instant payment system. Recipients can also use cash pickup or home cash delivery where available.

Xoom additionally lists international bill pay and mobile phone reloads. Cash pickup, home delivery and mobile-wallet payouts reach recipients who do not use a foreign bank account. By comparison, Venmo's international route reaches eligible non-US PayPal accounts for a 5.00% send fee ($0.99 minimum, $4.99 maximum) plus a 4.00% currency-conversion spread unless a lower spread is disclosed.

Xoom's homepage publishes no fixed fee table and notes that individual and aggregate transaction limits may apply. Before you submit a transfer, Xoom displays the exact fee and recipient payout in a quote.

Fees vary by country, selected features and other factors, and Xoom also earns revenue when converting currencies. Because Xoom's homepage provides no flat percentage or dollar table, compare a live Xoom quote directly against Wise's quoted total. Xoom fits cross-border cash pickup and wallet delivery rather than domestic US peer-to-peer splits; see the [Wise alternatives comparison](/alternatives/wise/) for additional cross-border options.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Several payment and banking jobs call for a different category of product:

- Business checking and treasury management sit outside peer-to-peer transfer schedules; see the [business bank accounts roundup](/roundup/best-business-bank-accounts/).
- Dedicated multi-currency comparison beyond Wise and Xoom lives in the [Wise alternatives comparison](/alternatives/wise/).
- Bank-specific Zelle dollar sending limits do not appear on Zelle's homepage or consumer fee FAQ, so check directly with your bank or credit union.
- Fixed Xoom pricing prior to running a quote is unavailable on Xoom's homepage because fees vary by country, selected features and other factors.

If your main question is whether to pay with credit or debit, read the [credit card and debit card comparison](/compare/credit-card-vs-debit-card/).

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Venmo Alternatives
alternatives.body:
A fee change could shift the lowest-cost route for the same transfer:

- Venmo changing its 1.75% instant-transfer rate or $25 cap.
- Linked banks introducing consumer Zelle transaction fees above the 99.40% fee-free survey share.
- PayPal adjusting its 2.90% + $0.30 card-funding rate or $0 standard bank withdrawal.
- Wise changing its 0.23% starting conversion floor or Venmo changing its 4.00% foreign-exchange spread.
- Xoom publishing a fixed fee schedule by country and selected delivery features.

For sellers comparing Square Plus against Square Free, include the $49 monthly location fee alongside the lower in-person and invoice card rates. Browse the [financial product comparison hub](/compare/) for other fee breakdowns.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Venmo Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Venmo fits domestic personal sends funded by a balance, linked bank account or debit card, each priced at $0. Its $0 standard bank withdrawal avoids instant-transfer charges when a one-to-three-business-day transfer works, and unlike Apple Cash it runs across both iPhone and Android devices.

For sellers whose buyers already pay with Venmo, the standard Business Profile rate is 1.9% + $0.10 per payment. Venmo's 1.9% + $0.10 rate sits below Square Free's 2.6% + $0.15 in-person card rate on the same ticket size, though Square accepts major cards from buyers without Venmo.

Venmo's debit card costs $0 to acquire or replace and charges $0 at US MoneyPass ATMs. Its Stash rewards offer up to 5% cash back at select brands (capped at $100 monthly, requiring $1,500 in qualifying monthly spend for the 5% tier). Check the fee on the transfer type you run most often before adding a second wallet.

verdict:
Zelle avoids a wallet cash-out for eligible domestic bank transfers. PayPal and Apple Cash offer other personal-payment routes, Wise and Xoom address international transfers, and Square prices business card acceptance separately from Venmo's Business Profile.

To compare Venmo alternatives for your next payment, write down the funding method, destination, payment type and required arrival time, then apply the matching fees in the table.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of Venmo?
faqs.answer: Zelle fits eligible US bank-to-bank payments, Apple Cash fits payments between compatible Apple devices, and PayPal fits wallet-based personal sends. Wise and Xoom cover international transfers, while Square handles business card payments and invoices. Zelle notes consumer sends and receipts are typically $0 and advises confirming with your bank or credit union.

faqs.question: Which Venmo alternative lets you move money to your bank account instantly for free?
faqs.answer: Zelle moves money directly between eligible US bank accounts, typically within minutes for enrolled recipients, with no separate wallet cash-out fee. Zelle states consumer transactions are typically $0, and a first-quarter 2026 survey found $0 send, receive and request fees at 99.40% of linked consumer checking and savings accounts. Venmo charges 1.75% for instant withdrawals ($0.25 minimum, $25 maximum).

faqs.question: Is PayPal or Venmo cheaper for sending money with a credit card?
faqs.answer: PayPal costs $14.80 on a $500 domestic credit-card-funded personal send (2.90% + $0.30) versus $15 on Venmo (3.00%), saving $0.20. On a non-PayPal debit card, however, Venmo charges $0 for eligible domestic personal sends while PayPal charges 2.90% + $0.30.

faqs.question: How do Venmo Business Profile fees compare with Square?
faqs.answer: A standard Venmo Business Profile payment costs 1.9% + $0.10, while Venmo Tap to Pay costs 2.29% + $0.09. Square Free charges 2.6% + $0.15 for an in-person card payment and 3.3% + $0.30 for an online or invoice card payment. Square Free has a $0 monthly software price per location.

faqs.question: Can you use Venmo or its alternatives to send money internationally?
faqs.answer: Venmo supports sends to eligible non-US PayPal accounts for a 5.00% fee, subject to a $0.99 minimum and $4.99 maximum, plus applicable funding and conversion charges. Wise lists currency sending or conversion from 0.23%. Xoom supports foreign bank deposits, mobile wallets and cash delivery options, but its checked homepage provides no fixed fee table.

title: Rocket Money Alternatives: Prices and Plans Compared
h1: Rocket Money Alternatives: Prices and Plans Compared
metaDescription: Rocket Money alternatives compared: Monarch, YNAB, Copilot Money, Simplifi, PocketGuard and Honeydue, with published plan prices and limits.
intro:
Monarch, YNAB, Copilot Money, Simplifi by Quicken, PocketGuard and Honeydue are six Rocket Money alternatives, and they differ mainly in whether they charge for budgeting, for subscription cancellation or for neither. At The Modern Wallet, we lay out the published plan prices and the yearly cost arithmetic so the difference between a free tier and a paid subscription is visible in dollars.

[Rocket Money](https://www.rocketmoney.com/) has three tiers: Free, Premium and Premium+. The free tier tracks subscriptions, upcoming bills, spending and net income, with up to two custom category budgets. Cancellation on your behalf, unlimited budget categories, financial goals, credit reports, account sharing and net worth tracking sit in the paid tiers, and Premium+ costs $15 per month and adds bill negotiation and the Rowan assistant.

Because a subscription tracker and a budgeting app solve different problems, the [budgeting apps for couples roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps-for-couples/) and the guide on [budgeting when prices keep rising](/guides/how-to-budget-when-prices-keep-rising/) are useful companions to the table below. Quicken already has its own page on this site, so see the [Quicken alternatives](/alternatives/quicken/) comparison for its desktop products.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Rocket Money Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with the job Rocket Money is doing. Its Free tier lists every recurring subscription, and the app contacts providers to cancel for Premium members. None of the alternatives below advertises hands-off cancellation on the pages checked, so a household that mainly wants someone else to cancel services is weighing a feature as well as a price.

Next, separate budgeting depth from subscription handling. Monarch, YNAB, Copilot Money, Simplifi and PocketGuard each emphasise budgets, cash flow or spending plans, while Honeydue emphasises sharing between two people. Rocket Money's free tier caps custom category budgets at two, so anyone who wants more than two categories has to compare the Premium tier against these apps.

Then compare billing units. Monarch, YNAB, Copilot Money and PocketGuard publish yearly prices that are lower than twelve months at the monthly rate, and PocketGuard adds a lifetime option. Simplifi's lower figure is a first-year offer, so the second-year figure matters.

Run through these five checks before picking an app:

- Does the household need cancellation done for it, or only a list of subscriptions?
- How many budget categories are needed, and does a free tier cap them?
- Is the app used by one person, a couple or a larger group?
- Which devices are in use: iPhone, Android, Mac or web?
- Is a yearly or one-time payment acceptable, or does monthly billing matter?

For a variable paycheck, the guide on [budgeting with irregular income](/guides/how-to-budget-with-irregular-income/) explains why a fixed monthly plan can break, and it applies to every app on this page.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Rocket Money Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Rocket Money fits households whose first problem is recurring charges they cannot see or stop. Its Free tier finds and lists subscriptions, and Premium members can have Rocket Money contact providers to cancel. Premium+ adds bill negotiation for services such as cable, internet, cell phone plans and home security, which none of the alternatives above lists on the pages checked.

Its free tier also costs $0 for spending tracking, bill tracking and two custom category budgets. Premium covers credit reports with weekly updates to a Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) Score 2 from Experian, financial goals that move small amounts into a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) insured account, and account sharing.

For someone who would pay $15 per month for Premium+ mainly to have a team negotiate bills, a $99.99 or $109 yearly budgeting app does not replace that service. The comparison depends on whether a saved bill covers the subscription fee, so the comparison rests on current monthly bills and the services that need handling.

alternatives.heading: Monarch Pricing, Plans and Household Features
alternatives.body:
Monarch is a subscription-funded budgeting and net worth app. Its pricing page lists $99.99 per year or $14.99 per month, a first week free and a money-back guarantee. The page also states there are never any ads and that Monarch does not sell financial data. A Plus tier adds forecasting tools, tracking for multiple income sources such as a small business and deeper investment tracking, though the pricing page checked does not list a Plus price.

Monarch also publishes a household concept, so transactions can be flagged as needing review and assigned to a family member. It recommends signing up on the web rather than through the Apple or Google app stores for easier subscription management.

The yearly math is simple. Twelve months at $14.99 costs $179.88, while the yearly plan costs $99.99, a $79.89 difference. Compared with Rocket Money Premium+ at $15 per month, which is $180 over twelve months, Monarch's yearly plan costs $80.01 less, though the two apps include different services.

Monarch falls short of Rocket Money on the pages checked in one respect: it does not advertise cancelling subscriptions or negotiating bills on a member's behalf. It fits households that want one paid app for budgeting, net worth and shared visibility.

alternatives.heading: YNAB Plans, Free Trial and Shared Subscriptions
alternatives.body:
YNAB, short for You Need A Budget, charges $109 per year ($9.08 per month) or $14.99 per month, plus tax where applicable. Its pricing page offers a 34-day free trial with no credit card required when signing up directly, and one subscription can be shared with up to six people.

The method is the product. YNAB asks members to give each dollar a job, which differs from the automatic categorization and subscription tracking that Rocket Money's free tier lists. Its pricing page says it makes money from the subscription price and nothing else.

A worked example for a two-person household shows the sharing rule. If two partners each bought a separate $109 yearly plan, the cost is $218. One shared YNAB subscription costs $109, a $109 difference. The monthly plan over twelve months costs $179.88, which is $70.88 more than the yearly plan, consistent with the $70 savings YNAB lists.

Where it falls short versus Rocket Money: the pricing page does not mention subscription cancellation or bill negotiation, and it has no free tier beyond the 34-day trial. YNAB fits people who want to plan spending in advance and are willing to pay for a method.

alternatives.heading: Copilot Money Single Plan and Assistant
alternatives.body:
Copilot Money sells one plan with no tiers, add-ons or AI credits. Its pricing section shows $109 billed yearly, which it expresses as $9 per month and marks down from $119. The plan includes connections to 16,000+ banks, a money assistant, iPhone, iPad, Mac and web access and support from real humans. The page lists partner invitations as coming this fall.

Because there is one price, the cost arithmetic is straightforward. At $109 per year, Copilot Money costs $9.08 per month on a twelve-month basis, which is the same yearly figure as YNAB. Against Rocket Money Premium+ at $15 per month ($180 per year), the yearly gap is $71. Over three years at the listed price, Copilot Money totals $327, versus $540 for Premium+ at today's rate, assuming neither price changes.

The pages checked list iPhone, iPad, Mac and web, and no Android app, so households that mix Apple and Android phones need to confirm device coverage. Copilot Money also does not advertise subscription cancellation on the page checked. It fits Apple device users who want a single clearly priced app with an assistant included.

alternatives.heading: Simplifi by Quicken Spending Plan and Pricing
alternatives.body:
Simplifi is Quicken's cloud budgeting product, separate from Quicken's desktop line covered on the [Quicken alternatives](/alternatives/quicken/) page. Its page shows $3.99 per month billed annually, against a listed $6.99 per month, as part of an offer for new memberships ordered by December 13, 2026. Quicken states that offers cover the first year only, that the subscription renews at the then-current rate, and that the final price may differ from the monthly figure multiplied by twelve.

Simplifi describes a Spending Plan that starts from monthly income, subtracts bills and subscriptions, and shows how much is left to spend each day. It also lists projected cash flow, savings goals and retirement planning.

At the promotional rate, twelve months at $3.99 is $47.88, while twelve months at $6.99 is $83.88. Against Rocket Money Premium+ at $180 per year, the promotional first year is $132.12 lower and the standard figure is $96.12 lower.

Simplifi falls short of Rocket Money on one point: it shows subscriptions and bills in its plan view but does not list cancellation on a member's behalf. It fits people who want a daily spending figure and a low published annual rate, with the renewal price in mind.

alternatives.heading: PocketGuard Premium Billing Options
alternatives.body:
PocketGuard publishes three payment routes for Premium: $74.99 yearly (shown as $6.25 per month, saving $81 a year), $12.99 per month, and a $149.99 one-time lifetime payment. Each carries a 7-day free trial. Its homepage lists web, iOS, Apple Watch and Android access and describes a figure for what is safe to spend.

The billing options make the math unusually concrete. Twelve months at $12.99 costs $155.88, against $74.99 yearly, a $80.89 difference. The lifetime payment of $149.99 equals just over two years of the yearly plan ($149.98 for two years), so the lifetime option costs less than the yearly plan from the third year onward if the price stays fixed.

Compared with Rocket Money, PocketGuard's pricing page shows a lower yearly figure than Premium+ at $180, but the services differ: PocketGuard's page does not list bill negotiation or cancellation on a member's behalf. It fits people who want a safe-to-spend figure and prefer a one-time payment to a recurring subscription.

alternatives.heading: Honeydue Free Shared Finance for Couples
alternatives.body:
Honeydue is a finance app for couples. Its homepage says it is the simplest way for couples to manage money together and lets each partner choose what to share. The homepage offers a free download and lists no paid plan, so the cost of the core app is $0 on the page checked. A separate joint banking program is listed as a waitlist.

The cost example is a comparison of a couple's yearly spend. Two people using Honeydue pay $0 for the app on the published page. Two partners on separate $109 plans from YNAB or Copilot Money would pay $218 a year, and a shared Rocket Money Premium+ plan at $15 per month would cost $180 per year, though Rocket Money's Premium account sharing and Premium+ extras are not available in Honeydue's free app.

Honeydue falls short of Rocket Money on subscription cancellation, bill negotiation, credit reports and net worth tracking, none of which its homepage lists. It is also built around two people, so single-person households get little from its sharing tools. It fits couples who want a free way to see agreed accounts together. For more on this use case see the [budgeting apps for couples roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps-for-couples/).

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
This page lists published prices and plan details. It does not rank apps for a particular household, and it is not financial advice. It is also not a source for investment, tax or credit decisions.

It is a poor fit for people who want an app that manages investments, files taxes or holds a bank account, because the products here are budgeting and tracking apps. It also skips apps with no public pricing page and products that have shut down.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Rocket Money Alternatives
alternatives.body:
A pricing or feature change could shift the lowest-cost route for the same household:

- Rocket Money publishing a Premium price or changing the $15 per month Premium+ rate.
- Monarch changing its $99.99 yearly or $14.99 monthly price, or listing a Plus price.
- YNAB changing its $109 yearly price or its six-person sharing limit.
- Copilot Money moving from one plan to tiers, or the $109 yearly price ending.
- Simplifi's $3.99 promotional rate expiring after December 13, 2026, or renewing above its listed $6.99.
- PocketGuard changing its $149.99 lifetime payment.
- Honeydue adding a paid plan.

For a variable income, the [budget variance guide](/guides/budget-variance-calculation-explained/) explains how to compare planned and actual spending when switching apps.

verdict:
Monarch, YNAB and Copilot Money cost roughly $99.99 to $109 per year on their published yearly plans, Simplifi lists $3.99 per month billed annually as a first-year offer, PocketGuard offers a $149.99 lifetime payment, and Honeydue lists a free app. None of them lists the cancellation on a member's behalf or the bill negotiation that Rocket Money includes in its paid tiers.

To compare Rocket Money alternatives for a household, list the current subscriptions, count the budget categories needed and apply the matching yearly price from the table. Then weigh any monthly fee against what a subscription audit would save.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of Rocket Money?
faqs.answer: Monarch, YNAB, Copilot Money, Simplifi, PocketGuard and Honeydue cover budgeting and spending tracking. Honeydue is free, PocketGuard offers a $149.99 lifetime payment, and Monarch, YNAB and Copilot Money publish yearly plans of $99.99 to $109. None lists cancellation on a member's behalf on the pages checked.

faqs.question: Is Rocket Money free?
faqs.answer: Rocket Money has a Free tier with subscription tracking, bill tracking, spend tracking and up to two custom category budgets. Cancellation on your behalf, unlimited budgets, financial goals, credit reports, account sharing and net worth tracking sit in Premium and Premium+. Premium+ costs $15 per month.

faqs.question: Which Rocket Money alternative is free?
faqs.answer: Honeydue's homepage offers a free download and lists no paid plan, and it is built for couples who choose what to share. Joint banking is a separate waitlist program. YNAB offers a 34-day free trial and PocketGuard a 7-day free trial, and both then charge.

faqs.question: Which Rocket Money alternative is cheapest per year?
faqs.answer: Simplifi lists $3.99 per month billed annually ($47.88 over twelve months) on a first-year offer for new memberships ordered by December 13, 2026. Its listed standard figure is $6.99 per month. PocketGuard's yearly plan is $74.99, and Monarch's is $99.99.

faqs.question: Can another app cancel subscriptions like Rocket Money?
faqs.answer: Rocket Money's Premium members can have it contact providers to cancel. The alternatives checked, Monarch, YNAB, Copilot Money, Simplifi, PocketGuard and Honeydue, do not list cancellation on a member's behalf on their pricing or home pages, so they show subscriptions while the cancelling stays with the member.

Trust & Will, Rocket Lawyer, FreeWill, ZenBusiness, Northwest Registered Agent and Bizee are six LegalZoom alternatives, covering online wills and living trusts, attorney memberships and business formation. At The Modern Wallet, we lay out the published price of each plan and the arithmetic behind it, so the gap between a $0 filing and a bundle with add-ons is visible before anyone checks out.

[LegalZoom](https://www.legalzoom.com/) lists an individual Basic Will at $129, a Pro Will at $149 and a Premium Will at $299, with couple versions at $229, $249 and $399. Its living trusts start at $399 for an individual, and a limited liability company (LLC) starts at $0 plus state filing fees, rising to $249 for Pro and $299 for Premium. LegalZoom also runs a holiday sale of up to 20% off a will or trust through December 13, so checkout prices can sit below the list prices shown here.

These services cover two different jobs, personal estate documents and business formation, and the right comparison depends on which one is on the table. The [first-time estate planning guide](/guides/first-time-estate-planning/) walks through which documents most households need, and the [will cost calculator](/estate-planning/will-cost-calculator/) puts a range on a will before any service is chosen.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a LegalZoom Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start by separating the personal side from the business side. Trust & Will and FreeWill cover wills and estate documents, Rocket Lawyer sells legal documents and attorney access by membership, and ZenBusiness, Northwest and Bizee focus on forming a business. LegalZoom sells all three categories, which is why a like-for-like comparison needs the right column of the table.

Next, compare what the headline price includes. LegalZoom's Basic Will at $129 lists a will, pet care provisions, online storage, 30 days of revisions and one printed set. Its Pro Will at $149 adds a healthcare directive, medical and financial powers of attorney, a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) authorization and 30 days of attorney consultations. Trust & Will's $199 Will Plan lists a will, a HIPAA authorization, a living will and a power of attorney in a single price.

Then add the renewal terms. LegalZoom's Pro Will consultations renew at $25 per month, and its Premium Will and Trust consultations renew at $199 per year. Its LLC Pro and Premium tiers renew at $49 per month for attorney consultations and $9.99 per month for bookkeeping tools. Rocket Lawyer's pricing is a recurring membership from the start.

Run through these checks before comparing totals:

- Is the need a will, a living trust, an LLC or several of them?
- Does the plan price cover one person or a couple?
- Are attorney consultations included, optional or a recurring charge?
- Are state filing fees, a registered agent or an EIN priced separately?
- Does the first-year price differ from the renewal price?

For the cost of the documents themselves, the [living trust cost calculator](/estate-planning/living-trust-cost-calculator/) and the [probate versus trust comparison](/compare/probate-vs-trust/) show what a trust adds. For a wider view of the category, the [best estate planning software roundup](/roundup/best-estate-planning-software/) covers more providers.

alternatives.heading: Trust & Will Plan Prices and Attorney Support
alternatives.body:
Trust & Will sells two core estate plans at flat prices: a Will Plan at $199 and a Trust Plan at $499. Its Will Plan lists a last will and testament, a HIPAA authorization, a living will and a power of attorney, while the Trust Plan adds a revocable living trust, a schedule of assets, a certification of trust and a trust funding guide. For situations such as special needs, blended families or high-net-worth estates, it lists attorney-led plans starting at $1,499.

An optional membership costs $49 per year and lists AI-powered answers, a secure digital vault and one free document shipment per year. Attorney support is a separate add-on of $299 on the Trust Plan.

A worked example shows the gap with LegalZoom. An individual living trust costs $399 at LegalZoom Basic and $499 at Trust & Will, a $100 difference. Adding Trust & Will's $299 attorney support brings the total to $798, compared with $549 for LegalZoom's Premium Trust, which lists one year of unlimited 30-minute attorney consultations renewing at $199 per year. The comparison above uses individual prices.

Trust & Will falls short of LegalZoom where a household also needs business formation, since it sells estate plans only. It fits people who want a flat-priced will or trust and prefer to add attorney support only if needed.

alternatives.heading: Rocket Lawyer Membership Pricing and Attorney Access
alternatives.body:
Rocket Lawyer sells legal help as a membership rather than a per-document purchase. Standard costs $149 per year or $34.99 per month, Plus costs $249 per year or $49.99 per month, and Pro costs $349 per year or $64.99 per month. Every plan starts with a free 7-day trial. Memberships list personalized legal documents, unlimited e-signatures through RocketSign, an AI legal assistant for questions and contract review, and attorney access. On Standard, Ask an Attorney is limited to 12 questions and Consult an Attorney Live is not included.

For business formation, members get their first LLC, corporation or nonprofit registration free of the service fee, then $99 plus state fees for each later one. A Legal Advice Session for privileged advice costs $149 for 30 minutes or $249 for 60 minutes.

The billing choice changes the cost. A Standard membership paid yearly costs $149, while twelve monthly payments of $34.99 come to $419.88, a $270.88 difference. Compared with a one-time $129 LegalZoom Basic Will, Rocket Lawyer's $149 first year costs $20 more but includes unlimited documents and signatures. Compared with the $249 LegalZoom Pro LLC, a Plus membership at $249 per year with a free first registration lists a similar first-year number before state fees.

Rocket Lawyer falls short of LegalZoom where a reader wants a single will purchase with no recurring charge. It fits people who expect to create several documents and ask attorney questions across the year.

alternatives.heading: FreeWill Free Will and Healthcare Documents
alternatives.body:
FreeWill lists its estate planning tools at $0. Its site says it never asks for a credit card or a fee to access documents, and it offers a last will and testament, an advance healthcare directive and a durable financial power of attorney. A revocable living trust is offered in California only. The service is funded by partnerships with nonprofits and businesses, and its page notes that one in six users include a charity in their will.

A worked example makes the difference plain. An individual will costs $0 at FreeWill against $129 at LegalZoom Basic, so the saving is $129. Two separate wills for a couple cost $0 at FreeWill against $229 for LegalZoom's couple Basic Will. Each person completing documents separately is the assumption here, since FreeWill's page does not describe a joint couple product.

FreeWill falls short of LegalZoom on bundled attorney access. LegalZoom's Pro Will lists 30 days of attorney consultations and its Premium Will lists a year, while FreeWill's page says online estate planning is not suitable for everyone and encourages people with complex needs to seek legal counsel. It also does not form businesses. FreeWill fits people with straightforward needs who want a no-cost will and healthcare documents, and who do not need a trust outside California.

alternatives.heading: ZenBusiness LLC Formation and Add-On Pricing
alternatives.body:
ZenBusiness lists LLC formation starting at $0 plus state fees, and prices most extras separately. Its pricing page shows Registered Agent service at $199 per year, an Operating Agreement Template at $99, an EIN filing at $99, Worry-Free Compliance Filings at $199 per year and Advanced Compliance Protection at $299 per year. Rush filing costs $79, and a domain name costs $25 per year. S corporation and C corporation filings also start at $0 plus state fees.

A worked example shows how the add-ons stack. Taking the $0 formation fee plus an operating agreement ($99), an EIN ($99) and a registered agent ($199 per year) comes to $397 in the first year, before the state filing fee. LegalZoom's Pro LLC lists an operating agreement and an EIN for $249 plus state fees, so the two routes land at different totals depending on which pieces are needed. With an illustrative $100 state fee, ZenBusiness comes to $497 and LegalZoom Pro comes to $349, though LegalZoom's page does not list a registered agent in that tier.

ZenBusiness falls short of LegalZoom for anyone who also needs a will or trust, since it covers business services only. It fits business owners who want a $0 formation fee and prefer to select each compliance service individually.

alternatives.heading: Northwest Registered Agent LLC Formation Costs
alternatives.body:
Northwest Registered Agent lists its LLC package at $39 plus state fees. The package page lists same-day processing, the use of Northwest's address instead of the owner's, local corporate guides, renewal reminders, registered agent service and free identity services. Its page also says state fees to form an LLC generally run $100 to $300 and that the formation filing typically costs around $100, with a range from $40 in Kentucky to $500 in Massachusetts.

A worked example uses an illustrative $100 state fee. Northwest comes to $139 ($39 plus $100). LegalZoom's Basic LLC comes to $100 ($0 plus $100) and its Pro LLC comes to $349 ($249 plus $100). The Basic route files the articles of organization only, so the $39 difference buys the extras Northwest lists, including registered agent service.

Northwest falls short of LegalZoom where a reader wants attorney consultations, trademark services or estate documents under the same account, since the page lists formation and registered agent services only. It fits business owners who want a low filing fee with a registered agent and mail address included.

alternatives.heading: Bizee Formation Packages and Free Registered Agent Year
alternatives.body:
Bizee, the service formerly branded Incfile, lists three one-time formation packages: Basic at $0, Standard at $199 and Premium at $299, each plus the state fee. Its pricing page says each package is eligible for one free year of registered agent service. The Basic package carries the lowest price for the core filing, and the higher tiers add services that Bizee lists on its package comparison.

A worked example with an illustrative $100 state fee puts Bizee Basic at $100, Standard at $299 and Premium at $399. LegalZoom's LLC tiers sit at $0, $249 and $299 before the same state fee, so on the headline numbers Bizee Standard costs $50 less than LegalZoom Pro and Bizee Premium and LegalZoom Premium both list $299 before state fees. LegalZoom's Pro tier lists an operating agreement, an EIN, 30 days of business attorney consultations and a year of document access, so the package contents differ and a column-by-column check matters more than the headline price.

Bizee falls short of LegalZoom for people who also want a will or trust, because it sells business services only. It fits business owners who want one-time package pricing and a first year of registered agent service included.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Several needs sit outside what these providers list:

- Estates with complex family or tax facts, such as special needs, blended families or high-net-worth estates; Trust & Will points these to attorney-led plans starting at $1,499, and FreeWill's page tells people with complex needs to seek legal counsel.
- Readers who need a living trust outside California without paying; FreeWill offers its trust in California only.
- Trademark, patent or copyright work, which none of the three formation services above lists on the pages checked; LegalZoom lists those separately.
- Anyone needing legal advice on a specific situation; these pages list products and published prices only. Rocket Lawyer separates legal information from advice and sells a Legal Advice Session at $149 for 30 minutes.

To size a plan before shopping, the [first-time estate planning guide](/guides/first-time-estate-planning/) lists the documents most households start with.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on LegalZoom Alternatives
alternatives.body:
A published price change could shift the lowest-cost route for the same documents:

- LegalZoom ending its up-to-20%-off holiday sale on December 13, which returns the Basic Will to $129 and the Premium Will to $299.
- Trust & Will publishing a couple price for its Will Plan or Trust Plan, or changing the $299 attorney support add-on.
- Rocket Lawyer changing its $149, $249 or $349 yearly membership prices or its $99 charge for later registrations.
- FreeWill adding a fee or extending its living trust beyond California.
- ZenBusiness, Northwest or Bizee changing a $0, $39 or $199 formation price, or moving registered agent service in or out of a package.
- Nolo's WillMaker pages becoming readable, which would add another will-software row to the table.

Browse the [financial product comparison hub](/compare/) for other fee breakdowns.

stillBetterFit.heading: When LegalZoom Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
LegalZoom covers both personal and business paperwork under one account. A household that needs a will and also plans to form an LLC can buy both there, with the same login, the same document storage and the same attorney network. Rocket Lawyer is the one alternative above that bundles documents and a first LLC registration, and it does so as a membership rather than as separately priced wills and trusts.

LegalZoom's tiers are also priced to bundle attorney access. The Pro Will adds 30 days of attorney consultations for $20 more than the $129 Basic Will, and the Premium Will adds a year of consultations, annual estate planning review and 10% off LegalZoom products. Its LLC Pro tier lists an operating agreement, an EIN and unlimited 30-minute attorney consultations for 30 days in one $249 package, while ZenBusiness prices the operating agreement and EIN at $99 each.

The holiday sale is a third factor. LegalZoom lists up to 20% off a will or trust through December 13, with a Basic Will at $116.10 and a Premium Will at $239.20 on the sale page, compared with the $129 and $299 list prices. A sale that ends can narrow or close a gap with a flat-priced competitor.

verdict:
FreeWill lists the lowest personal price at $0, Trust & Will lists flat $199 and $499 plans, and Rocket Lawyer prices a recurring membership. For business formation, Northwest lists $39 plus state fees, while ZenBusiness and Bizee list $0 base tiers with add-ons or paid packages. LegalZoom lists priced wills, living trusts and LLC formation as separate products on one site, while Rocket Lawyer bundles documents and LLC registration in a membership.

To compare LegalZoom alternatives for your own situation, write down whether you need a will, a trust or an LLC, whether the plan covers one person or two, and whether attorney consultations or a registered agent are needed. Then total the published prices in the table, including state fees and any renewals.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of LegalZoom?
faqs.answer: Trust & Will and FreeWill fit online wills and trusts, Rocket Lawyer fits people who want attorney access and unlimited documents under a membership, and ZenBusiness, Northwest Registered Agent and Bizee fit LLC formation. FreeWill lists its will at $0, Trust & Will lists a Will Plan at $199 and a Trust Plan at $499, and Northwest lists LLC formation at $39 plus state fees.

faqs.question: How much does a will cost at LegalZoom compared with Trust & Will?
faqs.answer: LegalZoom lists an individual Basic Will at $129, a Pro Will at $149 and a Premium Will at $299. Trust & Will lists its Will Plan at $199. The LegalZoom Pro Will includes 30 days of attorney consultations that renew at $25 per month, while Trust & Will lists attorney support separately at $299 on either the Will Plan or the Trust Plan.

faqs.question: Is there a free alternative to LegalZoom for a will?
faqs.answer: FreeWill lists a last will and testament, an advance healthcare directive and a durable financial power of attorney at $0, with no credit card required. Its revocable living trust is offered in California only. FreeWill's page encourages people with complex needs to seek legal counsel, and LegalZoom's Basic Will is listed at $129 for an individual.

faqs.question: Which LegalZoom alternative has the lowest LLC fee?
faqs.answer: ZenBusiness and Bizee list a $0 base formation package plus state fees, as does LegalZoom's Basic LLC. Northwest Registered Agent lists $39 plus state fees with registered agent service in the package. The state filing fee is separate in every case, and Northwest's page says it typically runs around $100, from $40 in Kentucky to $500 in Massachusetts.

faqs.question: Do LegalZoom alternatives include attorney help?
faqs.answer: Rocket Lawyer memberships list Ask an Attorney access, with live consultations on higher tiers and a Legal Advice Session at $149 for 30 minutes. Trust & Will lists attorney support at $299 on the Trust Plan and attorney-led plans from $1,499. LegalZoom's Pro and Premium tiers bundle 30-minute consultations. FreeWill, ZenBusiness, Northwest and Bizee do not list attorney consultations on the pages checked.

title: FreshBooks Alternatives 2026: Plans and Prices Compared
h1: FreshBooks Alternatives 2026: Plans and Prices Compared
metaDescription: FreshBooks alternatives compared: Wave, Zoho Invoice, Zoho Books, Xero, Invoice Ninja, Bonsai and Square, with published plan prices and card fees.
intro:
Wave, Zoho Invoice, Zoho Books, Xero, Invoice Ninja, Bonsai and Square Invoices are seven FreshBooks alternatives, with entry prices that run from $0 plans to Xero's $27 per month Early plan. At The Modern Wallet, we show the arithmetic behind invoicing and accounting comparisons so you can see what client limits, per-user seats and card fees add up to over a year.

[FreshBooks](https://www.freshbooks.com/) lists Lite at $23 per month for 5 billable clients, Plus at $43 for 50 clients and Premium at $70 for unlimited clients, with a Select tier quoted through a consultant. Credit card payments through FreshBooks Payments cost 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction, and Automated Clearing House (ACH) bank transfers cost 1%. Add-ons are priced separately: Team Members $11 per month per user, Advanced Payments $20 per month, and FreshBooks Payroll $40 per month plus $6 per month per user.

QuickBooks has its own page, covered in the [QuickBooks alternatives comparison](/alternatives/quickbooks/), and a price-by-users breakdown sits in the [QuickBooks vs FreshBooks comparison](/compare/quickbooks-vs-freshbooks/). For a wider shortlist of billing tools, see the [invoicing apps for freelancers](/roundup/best-invoicing-apps-for-freelancers/) roundup.

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a FreshBooks Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Start with the client count, because it sets the FreshBooks plan. Lite covers 5 billable clients, Plus covers 50 and Premium is unlimited. A freelancer with 12 clients lands on Plus at $43 per month, or $516 per year, while Wave Starter, Zoho Invoice and Invoice Ninja Pro list lower subscription prices for the same 12 clients.

Next, separate the subscription from the payment fees. FreshBooks, Wave, Square and the other tools that process payments each charge a percentage per card payment on top of the plan price. On a $2,000 invoice paid by card, 2.9% + $0.30 comes to $58.30, and 3.3% + $0.30 comes to $66.30. Bank transfers cost less: 1% of $2,000 is $20.

Then match the tool to the kind of record needed. Invoicing tools produce bills and track what clients owe. Accounting tools such as Zoho Books and Xero keep a full ledger with bank reconciliation. Bonsai sits closer to client management, with proposals, contracts and scheduling. For the ledger side, the [accounting software for freelancers](/roundup/best-accounting-software-for-freelancers/) roundup covers the bookkeeping options in more depth.

Run through these checks before comparing prices:

- How many clients are billed in a year, and does the count include archived clients?
- Will clients pay by card, bank transfer or both, and who absorbs the processing fee?
- Is a full ledger with bank reconciliation needed, or only invoices?
- How many people need a login, and is the seat price per user?
- Is payroll, mileage tracking or proposal software already paid for elsewhere? The [mileage tracker apps](/roundup/best-mileage-tracker-apps/) roundup lists dedicated options.

alternatives.heading: Wave Free Invoicing and Card Fees Compared with FreshBooks
alternatives.body:
Wave publishes a $0 Starter plan with unlimited estimates, invoices, bills and bookkeeping records, plus a mobile app and a single dashboard for cash flow and customers. Pro costs $19 per month, or $190 billed annually, and adds automatic bank transaction import, automatic merging and categorizing of bank transactions, receipt capture and automated late payment reminders. Wave Advisors, a done-for-you bookkeeping service, starts at $149 per month.

Online payments are an option on either plan. Starter lists 2.9% + $0.60 per credit card transaction and 3.4% + $0.60 per American Express transaction. Pro lists 2.9% + $0 per credit card transaction and 3.4% + $0 per American Express transaction, with a footnote that the $0 fixed fee applies to the first 10 transactions per month.

A freelancer sending twelve $2,000 invoices a year that all clients pay by card shows the gap. On FreshBooks Plus, the subscription is $516 and card fees are 12 x $58.30 = $699.60, totaling $1,215.60. On Wave Starter, the subscription is $0 and card fees are 12 x $58.60 = $703.20. The yearly difference is $512.40, almost all of it the subscription.

Wave falls short of FreshBooks on project tools, since Wave's pricing page lists no time tracking or project profitability reports. Wave fits sole proprietors who mainly need invoices and bookkeeping.

alternatives.heading: Zoho Invoice Free Plan Versus FreshBooks Lite
alternatives.body:
Zoho Invoice is a free invoicing application from Zoho, described on its pricing page as a forever-free solution for small businesses. It creates tax-compliant invoices, emails them or saves them as PDF files, and sends automated payment reminders. Its pricing page also lists limits of 2 users, 3 projects and 500 invoices per year, plus "Powered by Zoho Invoice" branding. It also covers quotes, recurring invoices, expense categorizing, time and project logging, customizable templates and a self-service customer portal.

One Zoho Invoice account can hold up to two organizations. Zoho lists free email and voice support at 24/5. Zoho states that data for a user inactive for over 180 days is deleted in the following 20 days after notice, so a dormant account needs a login or a backup to keep its records. Zoho Invoice's pricing page lists no payment-processing price.

For a freelancer with 12 clients, FreshBooks Lite covers only 5, which pushes the account to Plus at $516 per year. Zoho Invoice costs $0 for the same 12 clients. Even a freelancer with 4 clients, who fits inside Lite, pays $276 per year ($23 x 12) on FreshBooks against $0 on Zoho Invoice.

Zoho Invoice falls short of FreshBooks on accounting depth: the Zoho Invoice page lists invoicing, expenses and time logging, while ledger reports sit in Zoho Books. Zoho Invoice fits people who need a no-cost billing tool and who add payment collection through a gateway of their choice.

alternatives.heading: Zoho Books Plans for Accounting and Invoices
alternatives.body:
Zoho Books is Zoho's accounting product. Its Free plan costs $0 per organization per month and stays available as long as annual revenue does not exceed $50,000. Free allows up to 1,000 invoices and 1,000 expenses a year and includes one user plus one accountant, email support, mileage tracking, bank reconciliation, recurring invoices and 50-plus reports.

Standard costs $20 per month, or $15 per month billed annually, and allows 3 users and up to 5,000 invoices a year. It adds bank feeds, progress invoicing, sales tax tracking and application programming interface (API) access. Professional costs $50 per month, or $40 billed annually, for 5 users with inventory tracking, multi-currency transactions, timesheet billing and project profitability. Zoho Books has a 14-day free trial.

A business with $80,000 in revenue is above the Free plan's $50,000 threshold. Standard billed annually costs $15 x 12 = $180 per year, and billed monthly costs $20 x 12 = $240. FreshBooks Plus for the same year costs $516, a difference of $336 against annual Zoho Books billing.

Zoho Books falls short of FreshBooks on simplicity, since a full accounting system carries more setup than an invoicing app. Zoho Books fits small businesses that want a ledger, bank feeds and reports at a lower subscription price than FreshBooks.

alternatives.heading: Xero Plans, Invoice Limits and Pricing
alternatives.body:
Xero sells three plans in the United States (US): Early at $27 per month, Growing at $59 and Established at $97. New customers receive 80% off for the first 3 months, which makes Early $5.40 per month at the start, and the regular price then applies and auto-renews monthly.

Early covers quotes, 20 invoices, 5 bills, bank reconciliation, Smart Document Capture, real-time reports, sales tax and a 30-day cash flow forecast. Growing removes the invoice and bill limits and adds a 60-day forecast, performance dashboards and budgets. Established adds multiple currencies, project time and cost tracking, employee expense and mileage claims and a 180-day forecast. Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, costs $36 per month plus $6 per employee or contractor on any plan.

A business that sends more than the 20 invoices listed for Early needs Growing. At $59 per month, that is $708 per year, compared with $516 on FreshBooks Plus, a difference of $192. Established at $97 per month costs $1,164 per year against $840 for FreshBooks Premium. FreshBooks payroll lists $40 per month plus $6 per user, so Xero's payroll add-on is $4 per month lower at the base.

Xero falls short of FreshBooks on price for small client lists, since FreshBooks Lite is $4 per month below Early. Xero fits businesses that want a full double-entry ledger and forecasting tools.

alternatives.heading: Invoice Ninja Free, Pro and Enterprise Pricing
alternatives.body:
Invoice Ninja offers a Free plan at $0 per month with 5 clients and unlimited invoices. It includes 11 invoice templates, logo branding, online payments, recurring invoices, product and inventory management, projects with billable time, vendors and expenses, a client portal and deposits or partial payments.

Ninja Pro costs $14 per month billed monthly, with a $28 saving on annual billing (two months free). Pro adds unlimited clients and invoices, removal of the Created by Invoice Ninja line, automated late-payment reminder emails, reports on invoices, expenses and profit and loss, and automatic US state sales tax calculation. Enterprise starts at $18 per month for 1 to 2 users and climbs to $300 per month for 51 to 100 users, with permissions per user, bank account sync and e-invoicing access. Premium Business is custom, from $280 per year.

A freelancer with 12 clients passes the Free plan's 5-client limit and needs Pro. Billed monthly, Pro costs $14 x 12 = $168 per year, and billed annually it costs $140. FreshBooks Plus costs $516 per year for the same 12 clients, so Pro lists $348 lower on monthly billing and $376 lower on annual billing.

Invoice Ninja falls short of FreshBooks on payroll, since its pricing page lists none. Invoice Ninja fits freelancers who want invoicing, time tracking and expenses at a flat low price.

alternatives.heading: Bonsai Per-User Plans for Freelancers and Teams
alternatives.body:
Bonsai charges per user per month. Billed annually, Basic costs $9, Essentials $19, Premium $29 and Elite $49, with Elite requiring at least 3 users. Billed monthly, the same plans cost $15, $25, $39 and $59. Basic covers time tracking, task management, a customer relationship tool and unlimited clients and projects.

Invoices and payments start at Essentials, which adds proposals and contracts, forms, scheduling, a client portal, and expense and income tracking. Premium adds project insights, workload management, a deals pipeline, profit and productivity reports, removal of Bonsai branding and integrations with QuickBooks, Xero, Zapier and Google. Elite adds custom permissions, timesheet locking and a custom data import.

For a two-person studio on Essentials, annual billing costs 2 x $19 x 12 = $456 per year and monthly billing costs 2 x $25 x 12 = $600. FreshBooks Plus with one Team Member add-on at $11 lists $54 per month, or $648 per year. On Premium, the same two people cost 2 x $29 x 12 = $696 billed annually.

Bonsai falls short of FreshBooks on accounting: its pricing page lists income and expense tracking but no double-entry ledger, and per-user pricing grows with every added person. Bonsai fits freelancers and small agencies that want proposals, contracts and invoices together.

alternatives.heading: Square Invoices and Card Processing Rates
alternatives.body:
Square Invoices belongs to Square's plan structure: Square Free costs $0 per month per location, Plus costs $49 and Premium costs $149. Card payments made online or through an invoice cost 3.3% + $0.30 on Free and 2.9% + $0.30 on Plus and Premium. ACH bank transfers through an invoice cost 1% with a $1 minimum, capped at $10 on Plus and Premium. Manual card entry costs 3.5% + $0.15.

Square's invoice features include unlimited invoices, recurring invoices on daily, weekly, monthly or yearly schedules, batch invoices to multiple customers, milestone payment schedules, estimates that convert to invoices and reporting on what is paid, unpaid and overdue.

On a $2,000 invoice paid by card, Square Free charges $66.30 and Plus charges $58.30, matching FreshBooks' 2.9% + $0.30 at $58.30. Square Plus saves 0.4 percentage points on card volume, so $49 per month is recovered at $12,250 of monthly card volume. A $2,000 invoice paid by bank transfer costs $20 on Square Free and $10 on Plus after the cap, against 1%, or $20, on FreshBooks.

Square falls short of FreshBooks on accounting and expense features, since Square's pricing page focuses on selling and payments. Square fits sellers who invoice by card and bank transfer and also take in-person sales.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body:
Several bookkeeping jobs call for a different category of product:

- Bookkeeping done by a person is covered in the [bookkeeping services for small businesses](/roundup/best-bookkeeping-services-for-small-businesses/) comparison; Wave Advisors is the only listed service here, starting at $149 per month.
- QuickBooks is covered on its own page, the [QuickBooks alternatives comparison](/alternatives/quickbooks/).
- FreshBooks Select pricing is quote-based, so a Select-level comparison needs a consultant quote that this page cannot show.
- Business checking accounts and cards sit outside these tools; see the [business bank accounts roundup](/roundup/best-business-bank-accounts/).

If the question is which accounting tools suit self-employed filers, read the [accounting software for freelancers](/roundup/best-accounting-software-for-freelancers/) roundup.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on FreshBooks Alternatives
alternatives.body:
A pricing or limit change could shift which option costs least for the same client list:

- FreshBooks changing the 5, 50 and unlimited client limits on Lite, Plus and Premium, or its $23, $43 and $70 monthly prices.
- Wave extending Pro's 2.9% + $0 card rate beyond the first 10 transactions per month.
- Zoho Books moving the $50,000 revenue threshold on its Free plan.
- Xero raising or removing the 20-invoice limit on Early.
- Bonsai or Invoice Ninja changing per-user pricing or the 5-client Free limit.
- Square Plus changing its $49 monthly location fee or the 2.9% + $0.30 invoice card rate.

For businesses comparing paid plans, include card volume alongside the monthly price, since a 0.4 percentage point card-fee gap is worth $8 on a $2,000 invoice. Browse the [financial product comparison hub](/compare/) for other fee breakdowns.

stillBetterFit.heading: When FreshBooks Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
FreshBooks keeps invoices, estimates, proposals, expenses, mileage and time tracking in one subscription. Plus includes proposals and client retainers, and Premium removes the client limit entirely. A freelancer who bills by the hour, tracks time against projects and wants one login for the whole workflow gets all of that at $43 per month on Plus.

FreshBooks accepts credit and debit cards, ACH bank transfers, Apple Pay, Google Pay and buy now, pay later options. Its card rate of 2.9% + $0.30 matches Square Plus and its 1% ACH rate matches Square's.

The pricing page also lists a 30-day free trial and a limited-time 80% discount for the first 4 months, which puts Lite at $4.60 per month and Plus at $8.60 at the start. With that discount, a first year on Lite totals $202.40 ($18.40 + 8 x $23), and the client limit of the chosen plan decides whether a second billing tool is needed.

verdict:
Wave, Zoho Invoice and Invoice Ninja Free publish $0 subscription tiers, Zoho Books and Xero add full accounting at $15 to $97 per month, Bonsai prices by user, and Square prices by payment method. FreshBooks sits above most of them on subscription price, with client limits that set the plan.

To compare FreshBooks alternatives for your own invoicing, write down the number of billable clients, the share of payments by card, the number of people who need a login and whether a full ledger is required, then apply the matching prices in the table.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of FreshBooks?
faqs.answer: Wave, Zoho Invoice and Invoice Ninja publish $0 plans for invoicing. Zoho Books and Xero add full accounting, starting at $0 and $27 per month. Bonsai prices per user and bundles proposals and contracts, while Square Invoices prices by payment method. FreshBooks lists Lite at $23, Plus at $43 and Premium at $70 per month.

faqs.question: Is there a free alternative to FreshBooks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wave Starter costs $0 with unlimited invoices and estimates, Zoho Invoice is listed as forever free, Invoice Ninja Free allows 5 clients, and Zoho Books Free applies while annual revenue stays under $50,000 with up to 1,000 invoices a year.

faqs.question: How do FreshBooks card fees compare with Wave and Square?
faqs.answer: FreshBooks Payments charges 2.9% + $0.30 per credit card transaction, which is $58.30 on a $2,000 invoice. Wave Starter charges 2.9% + $0.60 ($58.60). Square charges 3.3% + $0.30 on Free ($66.30) and 2.9% + $0.30 on Plus and Premium ($58.30). FreshBooks and Square both list 1% for bank transfers.

faqs.question: Which FreshBooks alternative has no client limit?
faqs.answer: Invoice Ninja Pro, at $14 per month billed monthly, lists unlimited clients and invoices, and Bonsai Basic lists unlimited clients. Wave Starter lists unlimited invoices. FreshBooks limits Lite to 5 clients and Plus to 50, with Premium unlimited at $70 per month.

faqs.question: Do FreshBooks alternatives include payroll?
faqs.answer: Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, is an add-on at $36 per month plus $6 per employee or contractor. FreshBooks Payroll is $40 per month plus $6 per user. Wave, Zoho Invoice, Invoice Ninja and Bonsai list no payroll product on their pricing pages.

title: Wealthfront Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Plans Compared
h1: Wealthfront Alternatives 2026: Pricing and Plans Compared
metaDescription: Compare Wealthfront alternatives for 2026: Betterment, Schwab, Vanguard, Fidelity Go, Ally, Acorns, and M1 with published fees, minimums, and cash rates.
intro:
Betterment, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios, Vanguard Digital Advisor, Fidelity Go, Ally Invest Robo Portfolios, Acorns, and M1 are seven Wealthfront alternatives that provide automated investing or portfolio tools with published advisory fees from $0 up to 0.35% annually, alongside flat monthly subscriptions. The choice depends on whether an account requires tax-loss harvesting, human coaching, zero advisory fees, or a cash reserve with an annual percentage yield (APY). At The Modern Wallet, we lay out the published rates and account minimums so investors can compare annual costs without marketing spin.

[Wealthfront](https://www.wealthfront.com/) charges an annual advisory fee of 0.25% on its automated Wealthfront Portfolio, with no advisory fee on its self-directed Brokerage Account where clients can trade an exchange-traded fund (ETF) or individual stock. Wealthfront lists personal, joint, and trust taxable accounts, Traditional, Roth, and SEP retirement accounts, and 529 Education Savings Accounts. Its Cash Account lists up to a 4.45% APY (a base 3.55% APY as of November 13, 2026, plus an APY Boost up to a $150,000 balance) with zero account fees and up to $8M in FDIC insurance eligibility through program banks. Fees and prices across all providers are as published on each provider's site on November 17, 2026 and can change over time.
